subproblem.title: A good slice in a prescribed interval of levels (Markov choice of the slicing radius)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (domain univ) represented by an IMRep RT = (M, θ, ξ) in univ, RB = (M', θ', ξ') an IMRep in univ of degree m, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0, P_t ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) for t ∈ ℝ, and real numbers a < b. Assume (H1) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T); (H2) for L¹-a.e. t: P_t is integer multiplicity, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹(t) (P_t(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅), and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^m for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). Then there is t ∈ (a, b) such that P_t is integer multiplicity, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹(t), P_t satisfies the formula of (H2), and (b − a)·M(P_t) ≤ 2·(L·μ_RT({x : a < f(x) < b})) in [0, ∞] (b − a via ENNReal.ofReal, μ_RT = RT.measure).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (RT : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (RB : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Ps : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (a b : ℝ), RT.Represents T → Continuous f → a < b → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → AEMeasurable (fun t => (Ps t).massOn W) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (Ps t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * T.massOn W) → (∀ᵐ t, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m]) → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m]) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (b - a) * (Ps t).mass ≤ 2 * ((L : ℝ≥0∞) * RT.measure {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (good radii, Simon (8)–(10) and 4.10), for the strip W = {a < f < b}. Dependencies: markov_point, im_concentrated, imrep_mass (C1).
1. W := {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b} = f⁻¹((a, b)) is open (isOpen_lt with f continuous, intersected).
2. By (H1) for this W, g(t) := M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫⁻ g ≤ L·M_W(T). By (C1) for T and RT (univ is open), M_W(T) = μ_RT(W). Put I := L·μ_RT(W). Then ∫⁻_{Ioo a b} g ≤ ∫⁻_ℝ g ≤ I (setLIntegral_le_lintegral).
3. Let p(t) be the conjunction in (H2): P_t is IM, P_t vanishes off f⁻¹{t}, and the formula holds for all ω. By (H2), p holds for a.e. t. Apply markov_point to g, p, a < b and I: there is t ∈ Ioo a b with p(t) and ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·I.
4. Fix this t. By p(t), P_t is IM, so some IMRep R_t in univ represents it, and P_t vanishes off F := f⁻¹{t}, which is closed (preimage of a point under the continuous f). Since a < t < b, F ⊆ W. By im_concentrated (X = P_t, R = R_t, F, and the open set W ⊇ F), M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t) = g(t).
5. Hence ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·M(P_t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(b − a)·g(t) ≤ 2·(L·μ_RT(W)) (monotonicity of multiplication in [0, ∞]), and W = {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}. Together with p(t) this gives every clause of the conclusion. ∎
Remark: in the parent text the inequality M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t) is obtained with a smooth Urysohn cut-off; step 4 obtains the same inequality from (C1) through im_concentrated, which only needs that P_t is IM for the chosen t.
proof_key_steps: W = {a < f < b} is open and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T) = L·μ_RT(W) by (H1) and (C1).
markov_point gives t ∈ (a,b) in the a.e. set of (H2) with (b − a)·M_W(P_t) ≤ 2L·μ_RT(W).
P_t is IM and vanishes off the closed level set f⁻¹(t) ⊆ W, so im_concentrated gives M(P_t) ≤ M_W(P_t).

audit.reason: The open-strip integral bound, Markov selection, and concentration on the closed level set supply every conclusion with the correct constant. No boundary-representation hypothesis on RB is needed beyond the explicitly assumed slice formula.
